sections.label: 25-20.7-1-1. Application of Definitions
sections.text:
Title 25. Professions and Occupations
Article 20.7. Interior Designers
Chapter 1. Definitions
25-20.7-1-1. Application of Definitions

Sec. 1. The definitions in this chapter apply throughout this article.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-1-2. Agency
sections.text:
Title 25. Professions and Occupations
Article 20.7. Interior Designers
Chapter 1. Definitions
25-20.7-1-2. Agency

Sec. 2. "Agency" means the Indiana professional licensing agency established by IC 25-1-5-3 .
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-1-3. Applicant
sections.text:
Title 25. Professions and Occupations
Article 20.7. Interior Designers
Chapter 1. Definitions
25-20.7-1-3. Applicant

Sec. 3. "Applicant" means an interior designer who applies for a registration under this article.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-1-4. Are
sections.text:
Title 25. Professions and Occupations
Article 20.7. Interior Designers
Chapter 1. Definitions
25-20.7-1-4. Are

Sec. 4. "ARE" refers to the Architectural Registration Exam.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-1-5. Interior Design
25-20.7-1-6. Interior Designer
sections.text:
Title 25. Professions and Occupations
Article 20.7. Interior Designers
Chapter 1. Definitions
25-20.7-1-6. Interior Designer

Sec. 6. "Interior designer" means a person who practices interior design.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-1-7. Ncidq
sections.text:
Title 25. Professions and Occupations
Article 20.7. Interior Designers
Chapter 1. Definitions
25-20.7-1-7. Ncidq

Sec. 7. "NCIDQ" refers to the National Council for Interior Design Qualification.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-1-8. Nonstructural or Nonseismic
sections.text:
Sec. 8. "Nonstructural or nonseismic" means interior elements or components that:
(1) are not load bearing or do not assist in the seismic design of a building;
(2) do not require design computations for the structure of a building; and
(3) do not include the structural frame system supporting a building.
The term includes ceiling and partition systems that employ normal and typical bracing conventions and are not part of the structural integrity of the building.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-1-9. Reflected Ceiling Plan
sections.text:
Title 25. Professions and Occupations
Article 20.7. Interior Designers
Chapter 1. Definitions
25-20.7-1-9. Reflected Ceiling Plan

Sec. 9. "Reflected ceiling plan" means a ceiling design that illustrates a ceiling as if the ceiling were projected downward and may include lighting elements.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-1-10. Registered Interior Designer
sections.text:
Title 25. Professions and Occupations
Article 20.7. Interior Designers
Chapter 1. Definitions
25-20.7-1-10. Registered Interior Designer

Sec. 10. "Registered interior designer" means a person registered under this article.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-1-11. Space Planning
sections.text:
Title 25. Professions and Occupations
Article 20.7. Interior Designers
Chapter 1. Definitions
25-20.7-1-11. Space Planning

Sec. 11. "Space planning" means the analysis of design or spatial and occupancy requirements, including space layouts and final planning.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-2-1. Application of Article
sections.text:
Title 25. Professions and Occupations
Article 20.7. Interior Designers
Chapter 2. Registration Requirements
25-20.7-2-1. Application of Article

Sec. 1. This article applies to a person who practices interior design after December 31, 2009.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-2-2. Exemption From Article
sections.text:
Sec. 2. This article does not apply to an owner or employee of a manufacturing, wholesale, or retail establishment who provides consultation regarding interior decoration or furnishing:
(1) on the premises of the establishment;
(2) for purposes of an actual or prospective retail sale; or
(3) in the design, construction, ordering, or sale of:
(A) recreational vehicles;
(B) manufactured homes certified through the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development; or
(C) industrialized building systems certified through the department of homeland security.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-2-3. Exemption From Article
sections.text:
Sec. 3. This article does not apply to a person who:
(1) does not profess to be a registered interior designer; and
(2) is:
(A) an architect registered under IC 25-4 ; or
(B) a professional engineer registered under IC 25-31 .
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-2-4. Maintaining Electronic Registry
sections.text:
Sec. 4. Under IC 25-1-5.5 , the agency shall maintain an electronic registry of all interior designers who:
(1) electronically apply for and meet the registration requirements under this article;
(2) swear or affirm under penalty of perjury that the interior designer's representations and information provided to the agency are true; and
(3) pay the fees under IC 25-20.7-3 .
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-2-5. Electronic Registry
sections.text:
Sec. 5. Except as provided in section 8 of this chapter, the agency shall electronically register only an applicant who does the following:
(1) Electronically applies for the registration on a form prescribed by the agency.
(2) Meets the requirements of this article.
(3) Except as provided in section 6 or 8 of this chapter, passes:
(A) the examination administered by the NCIDQ; or
(B) the ARE.
(4) Pays the registration fee under IC 25-20.7-3 .
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-2-6. Examination Waiver
sections.text:
Sec. 6. The examination requirement under section 5(3) of this chapter is waived if the applicant holds a current certificate issued by the NCIDQ or documentation of the successful completion of the ARE.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-2-7. Qualifications for Registration
sections.text:
Sec. 7. To qualify for registration under this article, an applicant must not have a conviction for:
(1) an act that would constitute a ground for disciplinary sanction under IC 25-1-11 ; or
(2) a felony that has a direct bearing on the applicant's ability to practice competently.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-2-8. Registration of Applicants
sections.text:
Sec. 8. The agency shall register an applicant who:
(1) applies for registration under this article before December 31, 2011;
(2) meets all the registration requirements under this article other than the requirement under section 5(3) of this chapter; and
(3) meets one (1) or more of the following:
(A) Has:
(i) received at least two (2) years of interior design education; and
(ii) practiced in the field of interior design for at least ten (10) years.
(B) Has practiced interior design for at least fifteen (15) years.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-2-9. Registration Renewal
sections.text:
Sec. 9. The agency shall renew a registration of a registered interior designer only if the registered interior designer meets the following conditions:
(1) The applicant successfully completes the continuing education requirements under this chapter.
(2) The applicant pays the renewal fee under IC 25-20.7-3 .
(3) Except for an applicant who is registered under section 8 of this chapter, the applicant:
(A) has documentation of successful completion of the examination administered by the ARE; or
(B) holds a current certificate issued by the NCIDQ.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-2-10. Continuing Education
sections.text:
Sec. 10. A registered interior designer must complete at least twelve (12) hours of continuing education in interior design or a discipline related to the practice of interior design for the renewal of a certificate of registration under this chapter.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-2-11. Renewal Requirements
sections.text:
Sec. 11. A registered interior designer who continues to actively practice interior design shall:
(1) renew the registration not more than ninety (90) days before the expiration of the registration; and
(2) pay the renewal fee under IC 25-20.7-3 .
IC 25-1-2-6 (e) applies to the renewal of the registration of a registered interior designer under this article.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37. Amended by P.L.177-2015, SEC.44.

sections.label: 25-20.7-2-12. Application of Certain Rules
sections.text:
Title 25. Professions and Occupations
Article 20.7. Interior Designers
Chapter 2. Registration Requirements
25-20.7-2-12. Application of Certain Rules

Sec. 12. This article is not intended to relieve a registered interior designer from complying with any rule adopted under IC 22-13-2-13 .
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-3-1. Fees
sections.text:
Sec. 1. (a) The agency shall collect the following fees under this article:
(1) An initial registration fee of one hundred dollars ($100).
(2) A biennial renewal fee of one hundred dollars ($100).
(3) A restoration fee of one hundred dollars ($100).
(b) The fees collected by the agency under this article shall be deposited by the agency in the same manner as other fees collected by the agency are deposited.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-4-1. Renewal of Lapsed Registration
sections.text:
Sec. 1. A registered interior designer who fails to renew the interior designer's certificate of registration for a period of not more than five (5) years after the date the registration expires may renew the registration at any time within the five (5) year period after the registration expires by:
(1) electronically applying to the agency for renewal of the registration;
(2) completing twelve (12) hours of continuing education in interior design or a discipline related to the practice of interior design within the two (2) years immediately preceding the interior designer's application for renewal of registration under this section; and
(3) paying the biennial renewal fee and the restoration fee under IC 25-20.7-3-1 .
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-4-2. Lapsed Registrations for More Than Five Years
sections.text:
Sec. 2. After the five (5) year period referred to in section 1 of this chapter, the following apply:
(1) The agency may not restore the expired registration of an interior designer.
(2) To again be registered under this chapter, an interior designer must:
(A) make the same application to the agency as an applicant who has not been previously registered; and
(B) meet all the requirements set forth in this article for an initial registration.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-5-1. Prohibited Activities; Penalty
sections.text:
Sec. 1. (a) A person may not use the title "registered interior designer" or any title designation sign, card, or device indicating that the person is a registered interior designer unless the person is registered with the agency under this article.
(b) A person may not:
(1) present as the person's own registration under this article the registration of another person;
(2) make any false statement or representation or make a material omission of fact of any kind in obtaining a registration;
(3) impersonate any other registered interior designer; or
(4) use an expired, suspended, or revoked registration.
(c) A person who recklessly, knowingly, or intentionally violates this section commits a Class B misdemeanor.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-5-2. Person Allowed to Practice Interior Design
sections.text:
Title 25. Professions and Occupations
Article 20.7. Interior Designers
Chapter 5. Unlawful Practice
25-20.7-5-2. Person Allowed to Practice Interior Design

Sec. 2. This article does not prevent a person from practicing interior design if the person does not use a title or designation under this chapter.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.

sections.label: 25-20.7-5-3. Civil Judgments; Removal From Registry
sections.text:
Sec. 3. (a) If a civil judgment is entered against an interior designer by a court with jurisdiction in a civil judicial proceeding for negligence, recklessness, willful misconduct, or other breach of a standard of care in the practice of interior design, the interior designer must, within a reasonable time, remove the designer's name from the electronic registry maintained by the agency under IC 25-1-5.5 .
(b) An interior designer against whom a civil judgment described in subsection (a) has been entered may not be registered under this article.
As added by P.L.177-2009, SEC.37.
